answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: before an agent can transact, it must lock a nontrivial deposit of value in a shared vault, and that stake is slashed for provable misbehavior. Spinning up a thousand sybils then costs a thousand real bonds, making fake identities as hard to counterfeit as growing natural quartz overnight. Honest agents reclaim their collateral at the dawn of each settlement cycle, so the economic barrier filters out cheap fakes without punishing legitimate participants.
